1.n: Odysseus, left alone when Athena went to Lacedaemon (13.439–440)
the harbor of Phorcys, where the Phaeacians set him ashore (13.96)
root aorist: 'went up'; with the accusative of the way, ἀταρπόν
'path, track' (= ἀτραπός); accusative of the way traversed

2.n: ἀνά set between noun and adjective
= διά; διʼ ἄκριας 'through' or 'among the hill-tops' (Monro on 14.2); as 9.400, 10.281
'where, by which way' (dat. fem. of ὅς as adverb)
she showed him the way in 13.404–410

3.n: reduplicated aorist (πέφραδον) of φράζω, unaugmented: 'showed' (the way to) (Monro on 14.3, comparing 15.424)
δῖος ὑφορβός 'the brilliant swineherd', Eumaeus' epithet (again 48)
'swineherd' (ὗς + φέρβω 'feed'), by-form of συφορβός (Iliad 21.282; Odyssey 14.504); Eumaeus, not yet named
the article as relative (= ὅς); accent from enclitic οἱ
dative of interest with βιότοιο: Odysseus' substance
with οἰκήων (4): 'most of all the servants'

4.n: 'member of the household, servant' (οἶκος); epic gen. pl. -ήων; partitive with μάλιστα (3)

5.n: 'fore-house', the porch before the door of the hut

5.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. masc.

5.n: the walled yard of the steading (6–16), as the Cyclops' fold (9.184)

6.n: unaugmented (= ἐδέδμητο); ὑψηλὸς δέδμητο περισκέπτῳ ἐνὶ χώρῳ of Telemachus' chamber, 1.426
'seen from all sides', open all round; as 1.426, 10.211, 10.253
epic ἐνί = ἐν; between adjective and noun

7.g: with a clear space all around
7.n: two-termination adjective, with αὐλή (5): 'with an open space round it', serving as the glacis of the fortress, to guard against surprise (Monro on 14.7); 'with open ground all around' (Iliad 2.812)
the fold, object of δείμαθʼ (8); the relative clause becomes a new sentence in the English; accent from enclitic ῥα

8.n: on his own, as he bought Mesaulius (450)
= δείματο (τ → θ before the rough breathing of ὕεσσιν), unaugmented aorist middle: 'built for himself'
by-form ὗς (= σῦς); epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); dative of interest

8.p: verb · pres. part. mid. gen. sg. masc.
8.n: genitive absolute with ἄνακτος; epic gen. -οιο; the half-line again 450

9.n: 'apart from', without the bidding or help of; = νόσφι with movable ν; the line again 451

10.n: ῥυτός 'hauled', as 6.267 (Merry on 6.267); Monro on 14.10 takes it as 'quarried'
epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative of material with δείμαθʼ (8)

10.g: had topped it with a coping
10.n: 'set a coping (θριγκός, 7.87) on' the wall; in Homer only here
a thorny shrub, probably the wild pear; dative of material; in Homer only here

11.n: the stakes of a palisade, as Iliad 24.453
ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα 'this way and that', on either side

12.n: with σταυρούς (11); πυκνοὺς καὶ μεγάλους of stakes, Iliad 12.57
'close together, many' (plural only); μεγάλους in some manuscripts (Monro's critical note on 14.12)
the article marks a contrast, here between the darker and the lighter wood (Monro on 14.12)

τὸ μέλαν 'the dark part', the heart of the oak (Monro on 14.12); Aristarchus took it to be the bark, but Monro objects that the bark would hardly be called the black part of the wood, and that stripping it off would not be splitting

12.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
12.n: 'splitting off all round', so as to separate the softer outside and leave the heart (Monro on 14.12); epic -σσ-; in Homer only here

13.n: = ἔντοσθε with movable ν, + gen. αὐλῆς; 13–16 are almost a parody of the description of Priam's palace, Iliad 6.244–249 (Monro on 14.13–16)
epic form of δώδεκα; Priam's daughters had twelve chambers (Iliad 6.248)

14.n: neuter as adverb, + gen.; πλησίον ἀλλήλων of the chambers in Priam's palace, Iliad 6.245, 6.249
dative of interest: the sows of 15–16

15.n: σῦς is of either gender: here the sows (16)
'sleeping on the ground' (χαμαί + εὐνή), a feminine form; with σύες as 10.243
from ἐρχατάομαι, an epic by-form of ἐέργω 'shut in' built on ἔρχαται, ἔρχατο (73), with diectasis -όωντο; unaugmented; in Homer only here

16.n: fem. θήλεια 'female', in apposition to σύες (15)
'that have borne young, breeding' (τόκος); in Homer only here
epic τοί = οἱ; οἱ in other manuscripts (Monro's critical note on 14.16)
'the males', the boars; epic-Ionic ἄρσην (Attic ἄρρην)
unaugmented: 'lay', passed the night; the word does not necessarily imply sleep, as Iliad 9.325 ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον shows (Monro on 14.16)

17.n: epic πολλόν = πολύ, adverbial with the comparative: 'by far'
iter. (-σκ-) of μινύθω, transitive 'make fewer, diminish'; unaugmented; the iterative form only here

17.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
17.n: active participle with ἀντίθεοι μνηστῆρες (18) as subject, 'kept diminishing them by eating'; the English turns it: 'these kept dwindling, eaten / by the godlike suitors'

18.n: the heroic epithet, here of the suitors
unaugmented; 'send forth' (ἰάλλω 'send'); imperfect of what was done again and again

19.n: 'fat hog', as Iliad 9.208; partitive with ἄριστον

20.n: epic-Ionic τριηκόσιοι = τριακόσιοι; second accent from enclitic τε
τε καί joining the two numbers

21.n: epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); dative with ἐοικότες

21.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

21.n: epic αἰέν = ἀεί; ἐκτός in some manuscripts (Monro's critical note on 14.21)

22.n: Callistratus suspected the line for the counting of the dogs and for the epithet (scholia H X); Monro thinks it singular that the dogs are as many as Eumaeus' men (24–26), and that the line may once have referred to the swineherds, the lines that first named them being lost (Monro's critical note on 14.22)
ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν 'leader of men', a heroic formula (Asius, Iliad 2.837; Peisistratus, 3.454), given to Eumaeus here and often; Monro finds the epithet not unusual (critical note on 14.22)

23.n: unaugmented: 'fitted', i.e. made sandals to fit his feet; the leather he was cutting falls from his hand at 34

24.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

24.n: 'of good color' (εὖ + χρόα 'skin, color'); in Homer only here
οἱ ἄλλοι, Eumaeus' four men (25–26), who have not been mentioned: as the text stands, οἱ ἄλλοι is obscure (Monro's critical note on 14.22)

25.n: ἄλλυδις ἄλλος 'one this way, another that'
ἄλλυδις ἄλλος 'this way and that', as Iliad 11.486 and the other places

25.p: verb · aor. part. mid. dat. pl. masc.
25.n: syncopated aorist participle (ἠγρόμην): 'gathered' into herds; the half-line again 16.3

26.n: οἱ τρεῖς 'three of them' (Monro on 14.26), the article with the numeral
πόλις with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word

28.n: = ὄφρα; final, with the optative after a past tense

28.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

28.n: epic gen. pl. κρειῶν, with κορεσαίατο; for this form, in which the ει is unexplained, κρεάων can always be substituted (Monro's critical note on 14.28)

29.n: a kind of parody of the heroic epithets ἐγχεσίμωρος, ἰόμωρος; what precise meaning, if any, was given to the latter part of the word cannot be told (Monro on 14.29); cf. ὑλάω 'bark'; again 16.4

30.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
30.n: perfect participle with thematic (present) endings, probably the only Homeric form of the plural; the original κεκληγότες was later corrupted to κεκληγῶτες (Monro on 14.30); Aristarchus' two editions read κεκληγῶτες and κεκλήγοντες (Didymus, in Monro's critical note on 14.30)

31.n: 'sat down' on purpose, to quiet the dogs
the beggar's staff Athena gave him (13.437)

32.n: with the aorist indicative πάθεν: what would have happened
possessive ὅς 'his own' (= ἑός): by the steading of his own herdsman

33.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

34.n: the leather he was cutting into sandals (24) (Monro on 14.34); in Homer only here

35.n: with κύνας in apposition: 'them, the dogs'

35.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

ἄλλον Aristarchus and some manuscripts, ἄλλῃ the vulgate (Monro's critical note on 14.35)

36.n: 'thick, many': a volley of stones; epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν)

Odysseus, whom Eumaeus does not know: the narrator's word

37.n: adverbial genitive 'by a little', i.e. 'almost'; so only here in Homer
'tear apart' (διά + δηλέομαι 'hurt, damage'); in Homer only here

38.n: with the aorist indicative κατέχευας: what would have happened; accent from enclitic μοι

39.n: uncontracted (Attic ἄλγη); second accent from enclitic τε; ἄλγεά τε στοναχάς τε as Iliad 2.39

40.n: ἄναξ of a slave's master 'master' (4.87); genitive with ὀδυρόμενος καὶ ἀχεύων: 'for'

verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

'fat hog', a noun in apposition to σύας: 'fat swine'

42.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

47.n: epic -ππ- (= ὁπόσα); indirect question, with κήδεʼ

two-termination here, with the feminine αἰγός

the swineherd's name, given here for the first time
vocative in -α of a noun in -της

epic gen. σέθεν = σοῦ; genitive of comparison

59.n: Ionic -η: 'ours', a gift from slaves like us

Odysseus, not named; genitive with νόστον

a word of the Odyssey and the last two books of the Iliad; the meaning must be 'kindly, in gentle fashion', or else 'zealously'; the only clue to its derivation is ἀδευκής, which probably means 'harsh' (Monro on 14.62)

63.n: second accent from enclitic τε; explained in 64
'epic τε' in a statement of what is customary
uncontracted dat. -ῆϊ: 'member of the household, servant'

64.n: 'allotment' of land, as Iliad 15.498; second accent from enclitic τε
'much-wooed' (πολύς + μνάομαι 'woo'), as 4.770, 23.149: a wife whom many had sought

65.n: 'one who', the servant: relative with the subjunctive of a general statement
with ἀέξῃ, 'makes to grow onwards': ἐπί as in ἐπίδοσις (Monro on 14.65)

66.n: 'abide by, stay at' (ἐπί + μίμνω), + dat.; ἔργον ἀέξουσιν … ᾧ ἐπιμίμνω again 15.372

67.n: with the aorist indicative ὤνησεν: what would have been; accent from enclitic με
with the aorist indicative ἐγήρα: unreal condition

68.n: = ὄλετο (τ → θ before the rough breathing of ὡς), unaugmented 2nd aorist middle 'perished'
ὡς ὤφελλε + inf.: a wish that can no longer come true

in tmesis: ἀπὸ … ὀλέσθαι = ἀπολέσθαι; 2nd aorist middle 'perish'

69.n: lit. 'on the knees', used of utter downfall (Iliad 21.460), but here with a play on the literal sense: may the race of Helen be brought to its knees, even as she has loosed the knees of many men (Monro on 14.69)
in tmesis with ἔλυσε (ὑπολύω); the half-line again 236, of the expedition to Troy
in tmesis: ὑπὸ … ἔλυσε = 'loosed from under', i.e. killed; the subject is Helen

70.n: epic εἵνεκα = ἕνεκα; placed after its genitive Ἀγαμέμνονος
τιμή 'satisfaction' (compensation), as the Iliad's row (1.159; 17.92 'to win satisfaction for me')

71.n: 'so that', + optative after a past tense
epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative with μάχοιτο
optative of purpose after a past tense

72.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

72.n: unaugmented imperfect of συνεέργω (σύν + ἐέργω): 'held together', girding up the tunic for work

73.n: unaugmented; βῆ δʼ ἴμεν 'set out to go'
pluperfect passive of ἔργω (= ἐέργω) 'shut in', epic 3 pl. -ατο, as 9.221
'young pig, porker'; in Homer only here and 81

74.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

74.n: epic aorist ἔνεικα of φέρω (= ἤνεγκε); unaugmented
unaugmented (= ἱέρευσε); slaughtered for the meal

75.n: 'singed' the bristles off; second accent from enclitic τε; εὗσε A and Eustathius, εἷσεν the vulgate (Monro's critical note on 14.75)
'cut up small'; unaugmented; second accent from enclitic τε
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); καὶ ἀμφʼ ὀβελοῖσιν ἔπειραν Iliad 1.465, Odyssey 3.462
'pierce, spit'; aorist and imperfect coincide in this form

76.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

77.n: αὐτοῖς ὀβελοῖσιν 'with the spits as they were', without drawing them out of the meat (Monro on 14.77)
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); sociative dative with αὐτοῖς
unaugmented: 'sprinkled, strewed'; ἐπὶ δʼ ἄλφιτα λευκὰ πάλυνε Iliad 11.640

78.n: a rustic bowl of ivy wood (κισσός), as the Cyclops' (9.346); the line again 16.52
from κίρνημι, an epic present of κεράννυμι 'mix' (ἐκίρνα 7.182, 10.356, 13.53); unaugmented

79.n: neuter as adverb: 'opposite'; αὐτὸς δʼ ἀντίον ἷζεν as Iliad 9.218

79.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

80.n: the article as relative, subject of πάρεστι; antecedent χοίρεʼ (81); accent from enclitic τε
epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative with πάρεστι
'is at hand', singular with the neuter plural τά

81.n: = χοίρεα, neuter plural of χοίρεος 'of swine' (sc. κρέα): the meat of the young pigs (73), object of ἔσθιε (80); in Homer only here
'fat hog', a noun in apposition to σύας
marks the contrast with the porkers

82.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

82.n: 'pity' (ἐλεέω); again 17.451; the two accusatives are construed somewhat differently: 'not bethinking them of the judgment of the gods, nor (alive to) compassion' (Monro on 14.82)

'hostile, implacable'; δυσμενέες καὶ ἀνάρσιοι as Iliad 24.365
= τε; 'epic τε' after the relative, of what is wont to happen

86.n: root aorist subjunctive (ἔβην), with τε in a general relative clause

87.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

87.n: δέ τε, of what is wont to happen
οἶκον with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word

88.n: καὶ μέν takes up the sentence begun in 85 (Monro on 14.85)
'on them', dative of interest: the men of 85
objective genitive; ὄπις by itself in the sense of θεῶν ὄπις, as 82 (Monro on 14.82)

89.n: δὲ καί τι in this text; the vulgate δέ τι, which Monro thinks gives a less satisfactory meaning and makes τι a long syllable, and M δέ τοι, which he prints (Monro on 14.89 and his critical note)
'voice', some word from a god about Odysseus' death

90.n: epic κεῖνος = ἐκεῖνος: Odysseus; Monro joins κείνου λυγρὸν ὄλεθρον (Monro on 14.89)
in apposition to τι (89), what they know
= ὅτε, causal; Monro reads ὅ τε 'in respect that', 'as they show by the fact that' (Monro on 14.90)
'justly, as is right'; in Homer only here

91.n: = σφέτερα: their own homes and goods

92.n: 'tear apart, devour', of beasts at Iliad 11.479
= ἔπεστι, with the accent thrown back; οὐδʼ ἔπι the vulgate, οὐδʼ ἔτι a variant in Eustathius (Monro's critical note on 14.92)

94.n: οὔ ποτε 'never'; accent from enclitic ποθʼ
elided ποτε; τ → θ before the rough breathing of ἕν
dual of οἶος 'alone': 'two only'; δύʼ οἶα in the manuscripts (Monro's critical note on 14.94)

95.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
95.n: 'draw off' to the dregs (ἐξ + ἀφύω, a by-form of ἀφύσσω 'draw'); in Homer only here

96.n: 'substance, livelihood' (what one lives on), not 'life'; again 208; accent from enclitic γʼ

97.n: ἀνδρῶν ἡρώων 'of the heroes', partitive with τινι (96)
epic gen. -οιο; genitive of the space within which (Monro on 14.97)

98.n: 'twenty together' (ξύν + ἐείκοσι, epic for εἴκοσι); in Homer only here
φώς 'man'; genitive of possession with ἔστʼ (99)

99.n: = ἔστι; with the genitive φωτῶν (98): 'twenty men have not'
with καταλέξω; accent from enclitic τοι

102.n: hired men from outside, as against his own men; second accent from enclitic τε

a head of small cattle, here a goat

106.n: ὅς τις 'whoever, whichever', with the subjunctive of a general clause; masculine of the best he-goat
subjunctive without κε in a general relative clause

107.n: contracted acc. pl. (= σύας); feminine, as τάσδε shows

108.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

uncontracted -εαι (= δευήσῃ); epic δεύομαι = δέομαι 'lack', + gen.

511.n: genitive, with μὴ δεύεσθαι understood from δευήσεαι (510): 'which it is right that a suppliant should not lack'; the line = 6.193
= ἐπέοικε (κ → χ before rough breathing); impersonal: 'it is fitting'
'much-suffering'; in Homer only in the Odyssey

511.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

512.n: 'tomorrow morning' (ἠώς); second accent from enclitic γε

he must wear his own rags again: in the Iliad (4.472) the verb seems to mean 'knock aside' or 'against', and so a man may be said to knock about the clothes he wears; doubtless a colloquial word (Monro on 14.512)

513.n: 'for a change', spare (ἐπί + ἀμείβω); = ἀμοιβάς (521) (Monro on 14.521)

515.n: 515–517 are omitted in several MSS: cf. 15.337–339, where the lines are in place (Monro's critical note on 14.515–517)

517.n: epic -ππ- (= ὅπῃ); ὅππῃ σε κραδίη θυμός τε κελεύει as Iliad 13.784

518.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

519.n: the MSS here have οἰῶν, which Monro prints: the disyllabic οἰός, οἰῶν, required by the metre in most passages, come from ὀϝι-, and he thinks ὀΐων fictitious (Monro on 14.519)

520.n: = κατέλεκτο, root aorist middle (λέκτο) of καταλέγω 'lay down': 'lay down to sleep'; not καταλέγω 'recount'

521.n: a variant has μαλακήν 'soft' (Monro's critical note on 14.521)
= παρεκέσκετο, iter. (-σκ-) of παράκειμαι: 'used to lie by him', i.e. was kept in reserve; the reading of Aristarchus, the MSS being divided, some with παρεχέσκετʼ (Monro's critical note on 14.521)
'for a change' (ἀμείβω), = ἐπημοιβός (513) (Monro on 14.521); only here in Homer

522.n: infinitive of purpose; Aristophanes and Rhianus read εἴνυσθαι, the true Ionic form (cf. εἷμα) (Monro's critical note on 14.522)
+ optative of repeated action in the past
root aorist middle; optative of indefinite frequency

523.n: epic τοί = οἱ, with ἄνδρες … νεηνίαι (524) in apposition

524.n: 'young men', in apposition to ἄνδρες; Ionic νεηνίης = νεανίας

525.n: by-form ὗς (= σῦς); 'the boars', who slept outside (Monro on 14.525, referring to 16)

526.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
526.n: the going out properly follows the furnishing, but is put first as the main action (Monro on 14.526)
'furnished himself', took what he needed for his bivouac (Monro on 14.526)

527.n: = ῥα (enclitic ἄρα); accent from enclitic οἱ

527.p: verb · pres. part. act. gen. sg. masc.
527.n: a possessive genitive governed by βιότου, instead of agreeing with οἱ (Monro on 14.527)

528.n: one MS (F) has στιβαροὺς … ὤμους, perhaps rightly, since the dat. pl. in -οις is probably not Homeric; but the true reading may be στιβαρῷ … ὤμῳ, as in the recurring περὶ δὲ ξίφος ὀξὺ θέτʼ ὤμῳ, 2.3, 4.308, 20.125 (Monro's critical note on 14.528)
= βάλετο, unaugmented; in tmesis: περὶ … βάλετο

529.n: in tmesis with ἑέσσατο (ἀμφιέννυμι 'put on around')
= ἑέσσατο, in tmesis with ἀμφί; augmented aorist middle of ἕννυμι 'clothe' (= ἕσσατο), as Iliad 10.23
'warding off the wind' (ἀλέξω + ἄνεμος), two-termination; only here in Homer

530.n: epic ἄν = ἀνά; in tmesis with ἕλετʼ (ἀναιρέω 'take up')
= ἕλετο, unaugmented; in tmesis: ἂν … ἕλετο = ἀνείλετο
masculine with ἐϋτρεφέος μεγάλοιο: a he-goat

531.n: 'defender', in apposition to ἄκοντα; the half-line again 21.340

532.n: epic inf. (= ἰέναι); βῆ δʼ ἴμεναι 'set out to go'

532.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
532.n: 'going to lie down' (cf. κεῖμαι); Monro takes κείων as a future participle, always construed, as Homeric usage requires, with a verb of motion (Monro on 14.532); not κείων 'splitting' (425)

533.n: anastrophe (accent thrown back): πέτρῃ ὕπο 'under a rock'
epic gen. -εω (one syllable by synizesis), with ἰωγῇ
'shelter': Βορέω ἰωγή 'shelter from the north wind' (Monro on 14.533); only here in Homer
